title: Euro area unemployment, May 2026
question: What will Eurostat first publish as the euro area seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for May 2026, total sex, age 15-74, in percent of the labour force, rounded to one decimal?
resolutionSource: Eurostat euro-indicators unemployment release / une_rt_m data page
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first Eurostat-published May 2026 euro area seasonally adjusted unemployment rate in dataset une_rt_m / the corresponding euro-indicators release, total sex, age 15-74, unit percent of active population, rounded to one decimal. Use the first official print only; ignore later revisions to May 2026.
drivers: April euro area unemployment stable at 6.3%
Recent monthly range tightly clustered at 6.3-6.4%
Euro area unemployed persons fell by 84 thousand in April
Q1 GDP fell 0.2%, raising mild upside risk
Inflation and energy shock may slow hiring but layoffs are not yet visible

reasoning.text: Euro area unemployment rate, May 2026 first print

The target is Eurostat's first official May 2026 euro area seasonally adjusted unemployment rate, total sex and age 15-74, in percent. The April 2026 Eurostat release states the next unemployment release is on 2 July 2026, so that is the verified resolution date for the May 2026 first print.

reasoning.call: Opened Eurostat euro-indicators unemployment release dated 1 June 2026 for April 2026.
reasoning.result: Fetched April 2026 euro area unemployment rate 6.3%, March 2026 6.3%, April 2025 6.3%, and EU April 2026 6.0%.

reasoning.call: Read Eurostat table in the April 2026 unemployment release for recent euro area totals.
reasoning.result: Fetched euro area rates: Apr-25 6.3, Jan-26 6.3, Feb-26 6.4, Mar-26 6.3, Apr-26 6.3; fetched unemployed persons: Apr-26 11075 thousand and Mar-26 11159 thousand.

reasoning.call: Checked Eurostat euro-indicators listing for nearby macro releases and publication schedule context.
reasoning.result: Fetched official listing values: GDP Q1 2026 down 0.2% in euro area, employment Q1 2026 up 0.1%, May 2026 euro area inflation flash 3.2%, April 2026 retail trade down 0.4%.

reasoning.call: Opened Eurostat release calendar page for release-calendar provenance.
reasoning.result: Fetched calendar note that the release calendar uses Europe/Luxembourg time zone and the April unemployment release shows Next release: 2 July 2026.

reasoning.text: Base rate/reference class: monthly euro area unemployment rates usually move slowly at one-decimal precision; the last five official points shown for the euro area are 6.3, 6.3, 6.4, 6.3, and 6.3, making 6.3 the modal and median recent print.

The April level is stable year-on-year and month-on-month, while the number of euro area unemployed fell by 84 thousand from March to April. That argues against forecasting a near-term jump in the rounded May rate.

Counter-consideration: Q1 GDP contraction of 0.2%, weaker retail trade, and higher May inflation at 3.2% could weaken demand and push unemployment up. These forces justify keeping upside mass at 6.4-6.5 rather than making the interval too narrow.

Use recent monthly persistence as the anchor: median(6.3, 6.3, 6.4, 6.3, 6.3) = 6.3. Apply no directional adjustment because the April unemployment headcount fell but macro growth weakened. Set an 80% interval of +/-0.2 percentage points around 6.3, giving 6.1 to 6.5.
